description: One of the deals includes the rights to the Toys "R" Us and Babies "R" Us Canada names and logos. Another deal includes assets like inventory, leases and equipment, and the final transaction is for a lease at Vaughan Mills mall.
title: Toys 'R' Us Canada gets court approval to split business among 3 buyers

description: Nearly 30 years after Sarah McLachlan launched what would become the massively successful all-women touring festival, Lilith Fair, Rodrigo is starting a festival of her own. It's called Daisy Chain Fields, and it features an all-women lineup.
title: Olivia Rodrigo announces all-women music festival featuring Chappell Roan, Sarah McLachlan, Stevie Nicks

description: A trustee for the Canadian Museum for Human Rights says he has resigned from the Winnipeg facility's board over an upcoming exhibit about displaced Palestinians.
title: Human rights museum board member resigns over 'one-sided' exhibit on displaced Palestinians

description: The Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool on Washington's National Mall is set to be drained again for repairs after algae and peeling paint appeared just weeks ​after a $14.7-million US renovation, while U.S President Donald Trump threatened ​prison time for anyone caught damaging the pool.
title: Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool to be drained for repairs in wake of peeling paint, algae issues

description: For players and fans who have been around since Canada's men's soccer team's relative dark ages, the scenes and soundtrack in Toronto and Vancouver have been close to surreal. It wasn’t so long ago that home games felt like away games.
title: Canada's World Cup players relishing the support of loud, proud home crowd

description: A group of shareholders accused Uber Technologies management and directors of ignoring internal and external warnings about Uber's alleged failure ​to address sexual abuse by drivers. A spokesperson for Uber says the lawsuit ignores important facts.
title: Uber board sued over alleged failure to address sexual abuse by drivers

description: Montreal Canadiens goaltending great Carey Price was elected to the Hockey Hall of Fame on Monday. Joining Price into the class of 2026 are Patrice Bergeron, Pekka Rinne and Keith Tkachuk.
title: Canadiens great Carey Price elected to Hockey Hall of Fame

description: Montreal Canadiens goaltending great Carey Price was elected to the Hockey Hall of Fame on Monday, alongside Pekka Rinne, Keith Tkachuk and Cindy Curley in the player category.
title: Carey Price, Patrice Bergeron headline Hockey Hall of Fame's 2026 class

description: Tomato prices rose 45.2 per cent year-over-year in May, according to new inflation numbers released Monday. That's by far the highest price increase since May last year for any grocery item measured in the Consumer Price Index.
title: Tomatoes cost how much now? Why inflation has come for Canada's produce section

description: The Competition Bureau has obtained court orders requiring the parent company of Sobeys to produce documents and testimony for its investigation into property controls, which are agreements that can limit the places where a new grocery store can open.
title: Competition Bureau looking deeper into how Sobeys can control who sells food in your area

description: Jimmy Kimmel is taking a two-month break away from his late-night show and has tapped none other than comedian and Donald Trump’s longtime nemesis Rosie O’Donnell as one of several guest hosts taking the reins during his hiatus.
title: Jimmy Kimmel announces longtime Trump adversary Rosie O’Donnell to guest host during two-month hiatus

description: Clive Davis, one of the most influential people in the music industry and the record executive who helped bring Bruce Springsteen, Whitney Houston and Aretha Franklin into the spotlight, has died at the age of 94.
title: Music industry giant Clive Davis, who signed Bruce Springsteen and Whitney Houston, dead at 94

description: Ottawa Senators president and general manager Steve Staios confirmed Monday that the team's captain Brady Tkachuk asked to be traded, but did not reveal why.
title: Brady Tkachuk requested trade, Senators GM confirms

description: Two RCMP officers were shot and taken to hospital in Melville, Sask. after responding to an assault call, police say.
title: 2 RCMP officers shot by man in Melville, Sask., police say

description: Three people died due to extreme heat in France and ‌thousands of schools closed or modified timetables as European authorities issued heatwave warnings and forecasters in Britain said temperatures could smash records for June this week.
title: 3 deaths reported in France as much of Europe grapples with extreme heat

description: Abelardo de la Espriella, characterized by critics as far right, had earned the endorsement of U.S. President Donald Trump, who had said he would stop illegal immigration and crack down on crime and drugs.
title: De la Espriella's law-and-order platform wins Colombia vote after earning Trump's support

description: Toronto businessman Larry Tanenbaum's Kilmer Sports Ventures and the Detroit-based Ilitch Companies have officially bought into the Professional Women's Hockey League, being named strategic partners on Monday.
title: Toronto businessman Larry Tanenbaum's company invests $100 million US in PWHL

description: After days of heavy rain, the ongoing deluge has the City of Edmonton and surrounding communities contending with overland flooding, washed out roads, and wastewater systems pushed past their limits.
title: Deluge of rain leads to flooding, water restrictions in Edmonton and surrounding communities

description: Canada's annual inflation rate edged up to 3.2 per cent in May, according to Statistics Canada. Analysts polled by Reuters had estimated ​the annual inflation rate to touch three per cent in May, up ​from 2.8 per cent in April.
title: Canada's inflation rate rose to 3.2% in May, driven — again — by high gas prices

description: The Liberal government is weighing a significant routing change for the Alto high-speed rail project that would move the line's corridor south toward the shore of Lake Ontario, CBC News has confirmed.
title: Feds considering high-speed rail route change to include stop in Kingston, Ont.

description: A woman who raised more than $5,000 to take her terminally ill husband to a FIFA World Cup match in Vancouver says she has been unable to get wheelchair-accessible tickets through FIFA’s accessibility process.
title: Woman struggles to find accessible World Cup tickets for her terminally ill husband

description: Vice President JD Vance said Monday peace talks with Iran created a "good foundation for a successful final deal" to end the war that began at the end of February.
title: Vance says talks with Iranian officials set 'good foundation' for a deal to end war
U.K. Prime Minister Keir Starmer announces resignation, sets out timetable for exit

description: The family of a woman who lived with Alzheimer's is fighting for court-ordered restitution more than seven years after rings were stolen by a health-care aide off her arthritic finger at a Winnipeg personal care home.
title: Family of Manitoba woman still seeking restitution for rings stolen by care home worker

description: The House of Commons has wrapped for summer. What did Carney’s majority government prioritize, and what’s ahead for the summer?
title: Liberals push through bills as Parliament wraps

description: Thunderheart Tshakapesh spent nearly two years in the care of the province before being released after his 16th birthday. He was dead within a month. His passing kicked off a movement that led to a public inquiry.
title: 'No plan, no services, no support': How an Innu teen died after aging out of system

description: Mi'kmaw leaders gathered in Annapolis Royal this month to mark the 300th anniversary of the Peace and Friendship treaties and reflect on generations of legal battles that have been necessary to uphold hunting, fishing and self-governance rights.
title: 300 years after treaty signing, Mi'kmaw leaders say the fight for rights recognition continues

description: White nationalist groups often raise local issues in an effort to gain legitimacy, promoting extremist ideas and trying to recruit new members in the process, says a former neo-Nazi. Now a Vancouver-based anti-hate activist, Tony McAleer was interviewed by CBC News about Second Sons Canada's recent visits to northern Ontario.
title: A white nationalist group visiting Canadian locations is trying to normalize extremism, says a former neo-Nazi

description: When the federal government introduced supplemental health copayments for asylum seekers and refugee claimants earlier this spring, it also quietly brought in a 10-hour yearly cap on mental health sessions for them, CBC News has learned. Mental health practitioners have been lobbying for a reversal since, with limited success.
title: Ottawa cut therapy sessions for refugees to 10 hours per year. Now some are pushing back

description: A new naked-eye star was supposed to grace our skies in 2024, but it never happened. Astronomers say that it's still on the books and could even happen soon.
title: Remember that star that was supposed to explode in 2024? It didn't, but it could still happen soon

description: The debate over whether Canadians with mental illness should have access to a medically assisted death ramped up this past week raising questions around why it's so heavily scrutinized and who is most impacted.
title: Why the debate about MAID for mental illness still rages and where the conversation is at today
